Hi Amanda / team — Laura from Redwood security here. Quick answers to the questions Marissa summarized, plus attachments.

SOC 2 / HIPAA posture:
- Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II report (control categories: Security, Availability, Confidentiality). We provide SOC 2 summaries to customers under NDA and can provide the full report upon reasonable request.
- We support HIPAA-covered workloads and will execute a BAA for customers handling PHI. BAA execution is supported for Dedicated and Private deployment modes.

Deployment / PHI boundaries:
- Dedicated: Isolated tenant on reserved GPU pools. Good for PHI with strict data isolation and audit requirements.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full control over network boundaries and KMS; recommended for regulated, high-volume PHI.
- Hosted (shared multitenant API): Not recommended for PHI by default. We can discuss limited-scope exceptions, but those require an architecture review and additional contractual controls.

Technical controls / notes:
- Encryption: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest; customer-managed keys available in Dedicated and Private.
- Logging & retention: Application-level logging can be disabled for PHI scopes; audit logs available for Dedicated/Private with configurable retention.
- Access controls: RBAC and SSO integrations, MFA for console access; keystore/HSM options for key material.

Attachments (included): Redwood_BAA_Template.pdf; Redwood_SOC2-TypeII-Report-2025.pdf (summary link provided in body).

If you could share the vendor security questionnaire, I'll assign our security engineer to complete it. Also happy to do a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week to go over architecture and controls.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
